chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ur narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhal, from Thal'abah, from 'Umar ibn Aban al-Rafa'i, from Al-Subah ibn Sayyab, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, a man may love you and not know what you say about him, so Allah enters him into Paradise. And indeed, a man may hate you and not know what you say about him, so Allah enters him into Hellfire. And indeed, a man among you may fill his record with good deeds without any action of his own. I said: How can that be? He said: He passes by a group who insult us; when they see him, some say to others: 'This man is from our Shī'ah.' And a man from our Shī'ah passes by them, so they attack him and speak ill of him. So Allah, Exalted and Mighty, writes for him good deeds for that, until his record is filled without any action of his own.
ai.seo_question: How can a person's record be filled with good deeds without them performing any physical acts of worship?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith elucidates the concept of *imlā' al-ṣaḥīfah* (filling the record without personal action), where a believer's standing is determined by the community's collective praise or blame regarding their affiliation with the Imams. It underscores the theological weight of *Wilayah* and *Nasab*, illustrating how communal recognition of one's connection to the Ahl al-Bayt can accrue divine rewards or punishments independent of individual physical deeds.

en.basel-kadem: 39.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Sa’eed, the lessor, that he said: We were at the place of Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, and it was mentioned Zaid and those who went out (in rebellion) along with him. Some from the people of the congregation intended to (verbally) offend him, but Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, repelled him and said: At ease! It is not (permissible) for you to enter into what is between us, except through a path of goodness.

Indeed, no soul from us dies, except that happiness catches up to him before his soul goes out, even if by (the amount of) a hiccup of a camel. He said: And what is the hiccup of a camel? He said: Its milk.
